title: Physical vs Logical Architecture Comparison
prompt: According to Azure architectural principles, how is physical architecture distinguished from logical architecture?

options.text: Physical architecture refers exclusively to virtual machine operating systems, while logical architecture refers to network security groups.
Physical architecture manages user passwords, while logical architecture connects optical fiber cables between cities.
Physical architecture is configured via JSON templates, while logical architecture cannot be modified once created.
Physical architecture defines where Azure exists physically (datacenters, land, power), while logical architecture defines how resources are organized and managed (subscriptions, resource groups).

explanation: Physical architecture represents tangible assets (buildings, servers, network cabling, power), while logical architecture represents management boundaries (Tenants, Management Groups, Subscriptions, Resource Groups).

title: Azure Region Definition
prompt: What is the official definition of an Azure Region?

options.text: A software container hosting multiple Docker microservices.
A collection of Entra ID user accounts spanning an entire country.
A geographical area containing one or more datacenters connected through a dedicated, latency-defined network perimeter.
A single standalone physical server rack located in a customer data center.

explanation: An Azure Region is a set of datacenters deployed within a latency-defined perimeter and connected through a dedicated regional low-latency network.

title: Key Benefits of Azure Regions
prompt: What are the main benefits of deploying workloads across Azure Regions? (Select TWO)

options.text: Reduced Network Latency: Allows positioning applications physically closer to end users to improve response times.
Automatic conversion of Windows VMs into Linux containers without configuration.
Elimination of all Azure subscription billing charges.
Data Residency and Compliance: Enables organizations to keep data close to users while adhering to local privacy laws.

explanation: Azure Regions provide local data residency compliance and reduced network latency by placing cloud resources near users.

title: Availability Zone Definition
prompt: Which statement accurately describes an Azure Availability Zone?

options.text: A virtual subnet within an Azure Virtual Network used for database isolation.
A backup copy of data saved automatically in a secondary country.
A physically separate datacenter location within an Azure region equipped with independent power, cooling, and networking infrastructure.
A security group rule that blocks incoming HTTP requests.

explanation: Availability Zones are unique physical locations within an Azure region. Each zone is made up of one or more datacenters with independent power, cooling, and networking.

title: Matching Azure Physical Infrastructure Components
prompt: Match each Azure physical infrastructure component to its correct architectural description.

targets.label: Physically isolated datacenter facility within a region with independent power, cooling, and networking.
A discrete market (typically containing two or more regions) that preserves data residency and compliance boundaries.
Two regions in the same geography paired at least 300 miles apart for disaster recovery.
Latency-defined perimeter containing datacenters connected via dedicated low-latency fiber network.

explanation: Azure Physical Architecture builds from Datacenters -> Availability Zones -> Regions -> Regional Pairs -> Geographies.

title: Azure Regional Pairs Distance & DR
prompt: How far apart are paired Azure Regions typically located, and why?

options.text: Always in different continents, to enforce international border security policies.
10 meters apart, to maximize cable connection speeds between racks.
At least 300 miles apart, to prevent a single natural disaster or regional outage from affecting both paired regions simultaneously.
Exactly 5 miles apart, to allow wireless microwave synchronization.

explanation: Regional Pairs are separated by at least 300 miles (where possible) to protect against regional disasters, power grid failures, or natural events.

title: Azure Entra ID Tenant Scope
prompt: What represents the top-level logical boundary for organization identity, users, and authentication in Azure?

options.text: Resource Group
Storage Account Container
Azure Entra ID (Azure AD) Tenant
Virtual Network Subnet

explanation: An Entra ID Tenant represents a dedicated, isolated instance of Entra ID that an organization receives when signing up for Microsoft cloud services.

title: Management Group Capabilities
prompt: Which of the following statements regarding Azure Management Groups are true? (Select TWO)

options.text: Management Groups provide a scope of governance above subscriptions, allowing policy assignments to inherit down the tree.
Management Groups store virtual machine OS hard drive disk files directly.
Management Group hierarchies can support up to 6 levels of depth for enterprise organizational modeling.
Deleting a Management Group permanently erases all underlying Virtual Machines instantly without recovery.

explanation: Management Groups allow hierarchical organization of subscriptions (up to 6 levels deep) to apply Azure Policy and RBAC rules uniformly.

title: Azure Subscriptions as Boundaries
prompt: An Azure Subscription acts as a fundamental logical boundary for which two key functions? (Select TWO)

options.text: Physical Hardware Allocation Boundary: Used to assign CPU cores directly to server racks.
Billing Boundary: Used to segregate costs, group consumption metrics, and generate separate invoices.
Access Control & Security Boundary: Used as an administrative scope for applying RBAC role assignments and access policies.
Web Browser Session Boundary: Used to store user login cookies inside client web browsers.

explanation: An Azure Subscription acts as both a Billing Boundary (grouping usage costs) and an Access Control / Security Boundary (applying RBAC and policies).

title: Matching Azure Logical Hierarchy Levels
prompt: Match each Azure logical hierarchy scope to its correct management function.

targets.label: Individual manageable item in Azure, such as a Virtual Machine, Storage Account, or SQL Database.
Logical container that holds related Azure assets deployed, managed, and deleted as a lifecycle unit.
Logical container providing billing separation and top-level administration boundary.
Highest organizational scope used to manage governance and policy compliance across multiple subscriptions.

explanation: Azure Logical Hierarchy: Management Groups -> Subscriptions -> Resource Groups -> Resources.

title: Resource Group Rules & Properties
prompt: Which rule applies to Azure Resource Groups?

options.text: Resource Groups can be nested inside other Resource Groups up to 10 levels deep.
Deleting a Resource Group retains all child Virtual Machines running indefinitely.
A resource can exist in only one Resource Group at a time.
All resources in a Resource Group must be located in the exact same physical region as the Resource Group itself.

explanation: A resource belongs to exactly one Resource Group. Note that resources inside a Resource Group can reside in different Azure Regions than the group itself.

title: Azure Geographies & Data Residency
prompt: What is the purpose of an Azure Geography? (Select TWO)

options.text: To force all virtual machines in the world to reboot simultaneously.
To automatically translate English source code into 50 languages.
To ensure that geopolitical boundaries are respected for tax, legal, and compliance regulations.
To define a discrete market containing two or more Azure regions that preserve data residency and compliance boundaries.

explanation: Geographies contain two or more regions and ensure data residency, sovereignty, compliance, and latency boundaries are preserved.

title: Global vs Regional Azure Services
prompt: Which of the following is considered a Global Azure Service (not tied to a specific Azure Region)?

options.text: Azure Entra ID (Azure AD)
Azure Virtual Machine (IaaS VM)
Azure Managed Disk
Azure VNet Subnet

explanation: Azure Entra ID, Traffic Manager, Azure Front Door, and Azure DNS are Global services, whereas VMs, VNets, and Disks are Regional services.

title: Fault Domains vs Update Domains
prompt: In an Azure Availability Set, what is the difference between a Fault Domain (FD) and an Update Domain (UD)?

options.text: Fault Domains require paid licensing, while Update Domains are free for Linux VMs only.
Fault Domains protect against physical hardware failures (power & network switches), while Update Domains protect against planned maintenance reboots.
Fault Domains are located in different countries, while Update Domains exist inside user laptops.
Fault Domains manage software updates, while Update Domains protect against fiber optic cable cuts.

explanation: Fault Domains share common power source and network switch (protecting against physical hardware failure). Update Domains group VMs that can be rebooted together during planned Azure maintenance.

title: Availability Set SLA Guarantee
prompt: What is the Financially Backed Service Level Agreement (SLA) uptime guarantee for Virtual Machines configured inside an Azure Availability Set?
explanation: Azure offers a 99.95% SLA for VMs deployed across an Availability Set (protecting against single datacenter rack failures).

title: Availability Zone SLA & Requirements
prompt: Which of the following statements about Availability Zone SLAs and requirements are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Availability Zones protect applications from entire datacenter facility failures (power, cooling, flooding).
Availability Zones are only supported in single-core A-series Virtual Machines.
Deploying VMs across two or more Availability Zones in the same Azure region provides a 99.99% SLA uptime guarantee.
Availability Zones require connecting all servers to a 4G cellular dongle.

explanation: Multi-zone VM deployments provide Azure's highest single-region SLA of 99.99% by guaranteeing isolation across physical datacenter buildings.

title: Matching Resiliency Options to SLA
prompt: Match each Azure Virtual Machine deployment model to its corresponding Service Level Agreement (SLA) uptime guarantee.

targets.label: Virtual Machines deployed across two or more Availability Zones in the same region.
Two or more Virtual Machines deployed in an Availability Set (across Fault and Update Domains).
A Single Virtual Machine utilizing Premium SSD or Ultra Disk storage for all OS and data disks.
Application deployment replicated across paired Azure Regions for complete regional failover.

explanation: SLA Levels: Availability Zones = 99.99%, Availability Sets = 99.95%, Single Premium SSD VM = 99.90%.

title: Planned Maintenance in Update Domains
prompt: During planned Azure host platform updates, how does Azure use Update Domains (UD) to prevent application downtime?

options.text: Azure updates only one Update Domain at a time, allowing remaining VMs in other UDs to continue servicing traffic.
Azure automatically emails end users to log off for 4 hours.
Azure converts all Virtual Machines into static HTML files.
Azure reboots all servers in the datacenter simultaneously at midnight.

explanation: Sequential patching of Update Domains ensures that at least one instance of your application remains running during platform maintenance.

title: Hardware Failures in Fault Domains
prompt: If a top-of-rack network switch or power distribution unit (PDU) fails in an Azure datacenter, how does a Fault Domain (FD) configuration protect your workload?

options.text: VMs in the Availability Set are placed on separate hardware racks with redundant power and switches, ensuring unaffected VMs keep running.
The Azure subscription is transferred to a different billing account.
The Virtual Machines are instantly converted into Azure Functions.
The failed rack automatically downloads new RAM from the internet.

explanation: Fault Domains separate VMs across different physical hardware racks, power units, and network switches.

title: Resource Group Deletion & Lifecycle Rules
prompt: Which of the following actions happen when an administrator deletes an Azure Resource Group? (Select TWO)

options.text: Azure issues asynchronous REST API delete calls to remove all resources in parallel or proper dependency sequence.
The entire Entra ID Tenant directory is permanently erased.
The customer billing credit card is automatically charged  penalty.
All child resources contained within the Resource Group are automatically deleted as part of the lifecycle cleanup.

explanation: Deleting a Resource Group deletes all child resources within it. This makes Resource Groups ideal lifecycle containers for environment management.

title: Azure Resource Locks (CanNotDelete vs ReadOnly)
prompt: An organization wants to prevent accidental deletion of a critical production database while still allowing authorized applications to read and write data. Which Azure Resource Lock should be applied?

options.text: System Lock
Subscription Lock
CanNotDelete (Delete Lock)
ReadOnly (Read-Only Lock)

explanation: CanNotDelete lock allows authorized users to read and modify a resource, but prevents them from deleting it. ReadOnly lock prevents modifications as well.

title: Matching Governance Mechanisms
prompt: Match each Azure governance mechanism to its primary purpose.

targets.label: Grants fine-grained user identity permissions (e.g., Owner, Contributor, Reader) based on job roles.
Packages policies, RBAC roles, and ARM templates into repeatable subscription deployment standards.
Enforces operational standards and compliance rules (e.g., restricting deployment regions or SKU sizes).
Prevents accidental deletion of critical production infrastructure by administrators.

explanation: Azure Policy = Compliance rules; RBAC = Access control; Resource Locks = Accident protection; Blueprints = Deployment packages.

title: Cross-Region Replication with Regional Pairs
prompt: How do Azure Regional Pairs support business continuity during a widespread major disaster?

options.text: Azure forces all subscriptions to downgrade to free trial mode.
Azure sends printed paper backups of all SQL tables via express postal mail.
Azure automatically moves physical server racks onto cargo trucks to relocate them.
Azure prioritizes recovering at least one region out of every regional pair first to restore core services quickly.

explanation: In the event of a broad multi-region outage, recovery of one region from every pair is prioritized to ensure at least one region is restored rapidly.

title: Factors Influencing Region Selection
prompt: Which key factors should an architect evaluate when selecting an Azure Region for deployment? (Select TWO)

options.text: Data Sovereignty & Legal Compliance: Meeting local government regulatory requirements for data storage.
Number of employee parking spaces available at the local Microsoft office.
Feature Availability: Ensuring required Azure services (e.g. specific VM series or AI services) are available in that region.
Color of the physical datacenter building exterior walls.

explanation: Service availability, compliance/data sovereignty, latency to users, and regional pricing vary across Azure regions and must be evaluated.

title: Azure Sovereign Clouds
prompt: What are Azure Sovereign Clouds (such as Azure Government and Azure China)?

options.text: Gaming servers dedicated exclusively to Xbox Live multiplayer games.
Public Wi-Fi networks available at international airports.
Physically and logically isolated instances of Azure designed to meet strict government security, compliance, and regulatory requirements.
Free trial Azure subscriptions provided to university students.

explanation: Azure Sovereign Clouds (e.g. Azure US Government, Azure China 21Vianet) operate independently with dedicated isolated networks and compliance validation.

title: Role of Azure Resource Manager (ARM)
prompt: What is Azure Resource Manager (ARM)?

options.text: The central management and deployment service in Azure that provides a consistent management layer for creating, updating, and deleting resources via REST APIs.
A physical handheld device used by datacenter technicians to repair servers.
A desktop application installed on client PCs to play video games.
A third-party web browser for browsing external websites.

explanation: ARM is the management layer of Azure. Every request from the Azure Portal, CLI, PowerShell, or SDKs passes through ARM to be authenticated and executed.

title: Behind the Scenes REST API Flow
prompt: When an administrator clicks Create in the Azure Portal to deploy a Virtual Machine, what occurs behind the scenes?

options.text: The browser compiles C# source code and uploads a ZIP file to OneDrive.
The Azure Portal converts the UI inputs into an HTTPS REST API request sent directly to Azure Resource Manager (ARM).
The portal reboots the local client laptop to apply new Windows registry keys.
An email is automatically sent to Microsoft support staff to manually assemble a physical server.

explanation: The Azure Portal is a web GUI client. Behind the scenes, all Portal actions send REST API requests to ARM endpoints.

title: Characteristics of Azure Portal
prompt: Which of the following are key characteristics of the Azure Portal? (Select TWO)

options.text: Web-based graphical management console accessible from any modern browser.
Can only be accessed from computers connected directly to Microsoft headquarters Wi-Fi.
Requires installing a 50 GB local software package before opening.
Customizable dashboards allowing administrators to monitor and visually manage resources.

explanation: The Azure Portal provides a web-based GUI for building, managing, and monitoring cloud infrastructure across devices.

title: Azure PowerShell Syntax & Features
prompt: What naming convention does Azure PowerShell use for its cmdlets?

options.text: Verb-Noun syntax (e.g. New-AzVM, Get-AzResourceGroup, Remove-AzStorageAccount).
Python snake_case functions (e.g. create_azure_vm).
HTML tags (e.g. <create-vm>).
SQL query strings (e.g. SELECT * FROM AzureVMs).

explanation: PowerShell cmdlets always follow the standard Verb-Noun format, prefixed with Az for Azure cmdlets (e.g., Get-AzVM, New-AzResourceGroup).

title: Azure CLI Structure & Cross-Platform Support
prompt: How is an Azure CLI command structured?

options.text: git commit -m create vm.
npm install azure-vm-latest.
az <group> <subgroup> <action> (e.g., az vm create, az group list).
docker run -d azure-vm.

explanation: Azure CLI commands follow a clear command hierarchy: az + group + subgroup + action (e.g., az vm create).

title: Matching Azure Management Tools
prompt: Match each Azure management tool to its core description and command structure.

targets.label: Cross-platform command-line tool using az <group> <action> syntax (Bash, zsh, cmd).
Task automation framework using Verb-Noun cmdlets (e.g., New-AzResourceGroup).
Declarative Infrastructure as Code (IaC) files defining desired state deployments.
Web-based graphical user interface for visual resource creation and monitoring.

explanation: Management Tools: Portal (GUI), CLI (az commands), PowerShell (Verb-Noun cmdlets), ARM/Bicep (IaC files).

title: Benefits of Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
prompt: What are the main advantages of deploying Azure resources using Infrastructure as Code (IaC)? (Select TWO)

options.text: Automation and Speed: Allows rapid, repeatable deployments integrated into CI/CD DevOps pipelines.
Idempotency and Consistency: Ensures environments (dev, test, prod) are deployed identically without manual configuration drift.
Automatically increases internet connection speed at home by 10x.
Guarantees that no passwords or security keys are needed in cloud computing.

explanation: IaC provides repeatable, automated, consistent deployments with version control support.

title: ARM Templates Data Format
prompt: What data format is used to write native Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates?

options.text: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation)
CSV (Comma Separated Values)
XML (Extensible Markup Language)
INI file

explanation: Native ARM templates are written in JSON format containing schema, parameters, variables, resources, and outputs.

title: Bicep Language Purpose
prompt: What is Microsoft Bicep in relation to Azure ARM templates?

options.text: An antivirus program designed for Windows 11 PCs.
A domain-specific language (DSL) that uses cleaner, concise syntax to write Azure IaC, compiling directly into ARM JSON templates.
A video editing software included in Microsoft Office.
A database query language for querying MySQL tables.

explanation: Bicep is a transparent abstraction over ARM JSON that simplifies authoring experience with cleaner syntax and type safety.

title: Matching Azure CLI Command Groups
prompt: Match each Azure CLI command group prefix to the target resource category it manages.

targets.label: Manage Blob, File, Queue, and Table storage accounts.
Manage Azure Resource Groups containers.
Manage Azure Virtual Machine compute instances.
Manage Virtual Networks, subnets, and IP addressing.

explanation: CLI command groups align with Azure resource types: az vm, az group, az network, az storage.

title: Azure Cloud Shell Capabilities
prompt: What is Azure Cloud Shell?

options.text: A background virus scanner running on Azure datacenters.
A physical laptop handed out free at Microsoft stores.
An interactive, browser-accessible command-line shell pre-configured with Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, and common developer tools.
A paid third-party plugin for Microsoft Word.

explanation: Azure Cloud Shell is an authenticated, browser-accessible shell for managing Azure resources using either Bash or PowerShell.

title: Azure CLI Authentication Methods
prompt: Which of the following authentication methods can be used to log into Azure CLI? (Select TWO)

options.text: Sending a text message to a landline phone number.
Automated non-interactive login using Service Principals or Managed Identity in CI/CD pipelines.
Scanning a paper barcode on a physical ID card into a webcam.
Interactive user login via browser using az login.

explanation: Azure CLI supports interactive login (az login) for users, as well as Service Principal and Managed Identity logins for automated automation scripts.

title: Burstable CPU B-Series VM Family
prompt: Which Azure Virtual Machine family uses a CPU credit model that accumulates credits during low usage and bursts CPU performance to 100% during traffic spikes, making it ideal for web servers and development environments?

options.text: H-Series (High Performance Computing)
B-Series (Burstable CPU)
F-Series (Compute Optimized)
M-Series (Memory Optimized)

explanation: B-Series VMs accumulate CPU credits during baseline usage and burst up to 100% vCPU during high traffic periods.

title: General Purpose D-Series VM Family
prompt: Which Azure VM series provides a balanced CPU-to-memory ratio suitable for enterprise applications, relational databases, and medium-traffic web servers?

options.text: N-Series (GPU Enabled)
D-Series (General Purpose)
A-Series (Entry Level Basic)
L-Series (Storage Optimized)

explanation: D-Series offers balanced vCPU and RAM configuration for general-purpose server workloads.

title: Memory Optimized E-Series & M-Series VM Families
prompt: You are deploying a large in-memory SAP HANA or SQL Server database requiring up to 4 TB of RAM. Which VM series family should you select?

options.text: B-Series (Burstable)
E-Series or M-Series (Memory Optimized)
N-Series (GPU Enabled)
F-Series (Compute Optimized)

explanation: E-Series and M-Series VMs feature high memory-to-core ratios designed for heavy in-memory database engines like SAP HANA and enterprise SQL Server.

title: Compute Optimized F-Series VM Family
prompt: Which Azure VM series features a high CPU-to-memory ratio with fast processor clock speeds, making it ideal for batch processing, web analytics, and gaming servers?

options.text: B-Series (Burstable)
L-Series (Storage Optimized)
E-Series (Memory Optimized)
F-Series (Compute Optimized)

explanation: F-Series VMs have high CPU-to-memory ratios and high clock speed cores for CPU-bound computations.

title: Storage Optimized L-Series VM Family
prompt: Which Azure VM family includes direct-attached local NVMe storage providing high disk throughput and low latency for NoSQL databases (e.g. Cassandra, MongoDB) and data warehousing?

options.text: D-Series (General Purpose)
N-Series (GPU Enabled)
L-Series (Storage Optimized)
B-Series (Burstable)

explanation: Lsv2/Lsv3 Series VMs provide high-throughput, low latency, direct-mapped local NVMe storage.

title: High Performance Computing H-Series VM Family
prompt: Which Azure VM series features InfiniBand networking for ultra-low latency inter-node communication required by High-Performance Computing (HPC) workloads, scientific simulations, and weather modeling?

options.text: D-Series (General Purpose)
H-Series (HPC High Performance Computing)
A-Series (Basic Entry)
B-Series (Burstable)

explanation: H-Series VMs feature RDMA InfiniBand networking specifically engineered for complex parallel scientific and HPC simulations.

title: GPU Enabled N-Series VM Family
prompt: Which Azure VM family provides NVIDIA GPU acceleration for deep learning, AI model training, graphic rendering, and video editing?

options.text: E-Series (Memory Optimized)
L-Series (Storage Optimized)
D-Series (General Purpose)
N-Series (GPU Enabled)

explanation: N-Series (NC, ND, NV) VMs are equipped with NVIDIA GPUs for AI/ML model training, CAD rendering, and graphic acceleration.

title: Matching Azure VM Series to Workload Requirement
prompt: Match each Azure Virtual Machine family series to its intended workload optimization target.

targets.label: Memory-optimized workload (e.g. SAP HANA, heavy relational SQL databases).
High-performance computing workload (e.g. InfiniBand scientific simulations).
Compute-optimized workload (e.g. high-speed batch processing, web analytics).
Burstable CPU workload (e.g. low-traffic web servers, dev/test environments).

explanation: VM Series: B = Burstable, E = Memory, F = Compute, H = HPC.

title: Components Created During VM Provisioning
prompt: When creating a Virtual Machine in Azure, which additional child resources are typically provisioned automatically alongside the VM compute instance? (Select TWO)

options.text: Network Interface (NIC) connected to a Virtual Network Subnet.
An Azure Synapse Analytics dedicated SQL pool.
A physical optical fiber cable delivered to the customer office.
Managed OS Disk (Premium SSD, Standard SSD, or HDD) storing the operating system.

explanation: Deploying an Azure VM provisions underlying resources: Virtual Machine, Network Interface (NIC), OS Disk, Network Security Group (NSG), and optional Public IP.

title: Managed Disks vs Unmanaged Disks
prompt: What is the primary benefit of using Azure Managed Disks over legacy Unmanaged Disks?

options.text: Azure automatically handles storage account creation, scaling, and fault domain alignment without manual VHD file management.
Managed Disks convert all Windows VMs into Mac computers.
Managed Disks bypass all password requirements.
Managed Disks eliminate the need to pay for any cloud storage usage.

explanation: Managed Disks are managed by Azure behind the scenes, eliminating storage account limits and ensuring disks for Availability Set VMs are placed on distinct storage Fault Domains.

title: Matching Azure Disk Storage Tiers
prompt: Match each Azure Managed Disk storage tier to its performance and workload profile.

targets.label: Top-tier sub-millisecond latency storage for mission-critical I/O intensive databases (up to 160,000 IOPS).
Magnetic platter storage suitable for non-critical backup data and infrequently accessed storage.
High-performance SSD storage for production workloads and SQL databases requiring single-digit ms latency.
Cost-effective SSD storage for entry-level web servers, light workloads, and dev/test environments.

explanation: Disk Tiers: Ultra Disk (highest IOPS/sub-ms) -> Premium SSD (production) -> Standard SSD (dev/test) -> Standard HDD (backups).

title: Azure VM Scale Sets (VMSS) Purpose
prompt: What is Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS)?

options.text: An Azure compute resource that lets you create and manage a group of identical, load-balanced VMs that automatically scale in response to demand.
A physical scale used to weigh server racks inside datacenters.
A billing calculator for predicting Azure expenses.
A backup tool for printing hard copies of database tables.

explanation: VM Scale Sets allow auto-scaling identical VM instances up or down based on CPU, memory, or custom metrics, integrated with Load Balancers.

title: Azure VM Cost Optimization Strategies
prompt: Which of the following strategies can organizations implement to reduce Azure Virtual Machine compute costs? (Select TWO)

options.text: Azure Spot VMs: Utilizing unused Azure compute capacity at steep discounts for interruptible workloads.
Running all VMs at 100% CPU utilization 24 hours a day without stopping.
Deleting the billing address from the Azure portal user account.
Azure Reserved VM Instances (RI): Committing to 1-year or 3-year plans for up to 72% cost savings compared to pay-as-you-go pricing.

explanation: Reserved Instances (1-3 yr commitment) and Spot VMs (interruptible capacity) provide significant cost reductions for Azure compute.
